question.text: Scenario: Arjun Malhotra is preparing a PESTLE analysis of an industry he covers. Among the facts he has compiled are the following: the central government is promoting domestic manufacturing in the sector through a production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme; the country is a major exporter of the sector's products, supplying customers in more than 200 countries with annual exports in the tens of billions of US dollars; rising health consciousness and an ageing population are increasing demand for the sector's products; digital health, telemedicine, and AI-driven research are opening up new opportunities; a specific regulatory order issued by the government caps prices of essential products in the sector; and the sector faces growing emphasis on green chemistry, sustainable manufacturing, and effluent treatment compliance. Question 2 of 5: The country being a leading global exporter of the sector's products, with significant export revenue across many countries, represents which PESTLE factor?

answer.text: Economic — exports and global trade position are economic factors

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM Research Analyst workbook lists exports, imports, GDP, balance of payments, exchange rates, and domestic manufacturing among Economic factors in PESTLE. A country's position as a leading exporter with large foreign-exchange earnings is therefore an Economic factor. The Trap: Political covers policy and legislation, not trade volumes. Socio-cultural would cover demographics and lifestyle drivers, and Environmental covers ecological factors such as green chemistry and effluent treatment. Note: Category labels stripped from the scenario; pharma-specific 60%/USD 27 billion statistics generalised because the workbook pages checked did not carry those figures. Role-specific pro-tip label removed.
